## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammataṇhāabyākatātikathā* (Kv 13.9) is a debate text preserved in the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The controversy addresses the proposition that craving for mental phenomena or teachings (*dhammataṇhā*) is indeterminate or morally undeclared (*abyākatā*) [Catalog; Dube 1980]. In his survey of psycho-ethical controversies in early Buddhist schools, S. N. Dube cites the text and its commentary (*Kathāvatthu-Aṭṭhakathā*) under this proposition [Dube 1980]. SuttaCentral highlights doctrinal thematic ties with the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta* (DN 22) as well as the adjoining debate in the collection, the *Dhammataṇhānadukkhasamudayotikathā* (Kv 13.10), and lists one translation in one language [SuttaCentral].

While SuttaCentral lists no direct external parallels [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus analysis reveals extensive internal Pali text reuse across 15 canonical and post-canonical works [DharmaNexus]. Its largest reuse partner is the immediately subsequent *Kathāvatthu* debate, Kv 13.10, sharing 19 matching passages (covering segments §1.5–9.7 with §1.4–7.7) [DharmaNexus]. Further notable Pali parallels and shared formulas occur in the *Yamaka* (Ya 9.1.2), other *Kathāvatthu* debates (Kv 11.1, Kv 8.9, Kv 22.7, Kv 14.8), the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56), and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Across corpora, DharmaNexus detects conceptual and formulaic alignments with Sanskrit texts including Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā* and the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, the Tibetan *Vinayapraśnaṭīkā* (D 4135), and the Chinese *Yuanqi jing* (T 124) [DharmaNexus].
